card.intuition: A permission mode is the permission-gating slice of an agent mode: which tool calls trigger a permission request and which run automatically. Harnesses ship a ladder - read-only (reads auto, writes blocked), default (reads auto, writes ask), auto-edit, and full-auto.
card.analogy: A building's key hierarchy: pulling a public notice is free, editing a file needs a desk key, and only the facilities key opens the server room - you pick the rung that fits the job and the trust.
card.time_complexity: Every tool call costs an extra model provider request, because the tool result must go back to the model before it can decide what to do next - a too-tight mode adds human interruptions on top.
card.space_complexity: Approval and denial outcomes land in the context window as tool results and compete for the finite token budget, alongside everything else the session has read.
when_to_use: When the agent pauses on every harmless read - loosen the mode for read-only tools and keep prompting on writes and shell
When you want a research or planning session - a read-only mode blocks edits entirely
When the loose end must stay contained - run full-auto only inside a sandbox
gotchas: Too tight, you become the bottleneck: the agent stops every few seconds and approvals become rubber-stamps that mean nothing
Too loose, the agent edits files and runs commands you'd have wanted to see first
Approving on autopilot is the worst of both worlds - all the interruption, none of the protection

steps.label: Ladder
steps.annotation: The ladder runs from read-only, through default and auto-edit, to full-auto.

steps.label: Reads
steps.annotation: Reads are auto-approved in every mode; writes and shell are the variable part.

steps.label: Block
steps.annotation: Read-only and plan modes block writes and shell entirely.

steps.label: Ask
steps.annotation: Default mode runs reads automatically and asks before writes and shell commands.

steps.label: Auto
steps.annotation: Auto-edit and bypass modes reduce prompting, most defensible inside a sandbox.

exercise.prompt: Implement a permission mode gate. Read-only mode auto-approves reads and blocks writes; bypass only goes fully auto inside a sandbox.
hints: Read-only mode approves only read actions
The bypass branch ends the ladder - but safety only comes from the sandbox flag
exercise.test_code:
assert may_run('read-only', 'read') is True
assert may_run('read-only', 'write') is False
assert may_run('default', 'write') is False
assert may_run('bypass', 'write') is False
assert may_run('bypass', 'write', in_sandbox=True) is True
print('PASS')
